newsitem.title: UK: Unigate starts new year "reasonably well".
newsitem.headline: Unigate starts new year "reasonably well".

text.p: British dairy and distribution company Unigate Plc said on Monday that while it expected its markets to remain very competitive, it had started the new year "reasonably well".

The company added that sales and profits for the first two months of the year were ahead of last year and reported a 3.4 percent increase in its pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits to 129.6 million pounds for the year to March 31, 1997.
The improved results reflected a tight control of costs and contributions made by the group's acquisitions, said Unigate chief executive Ross Buckland in a statement.
"These results were achieved despite the difficulties caused by the weakness of butter and milk powder markets and the rise in the value of sterling," he added.

Unigate sales rose by 13.1 percent to 2.4 billion pounds ($3.9 billion). Profits from its European food division rose 19.7 percent to 100.9 million but dairy saw operating profits fall 22.6 percent to 34.5 million.
Compared with last year, lower prices for butter and milk powder reduced operating profit by about 12 million pounds.
Trading profits from the group's distribution arm Wincanton rose only 1.7 percent to 23.4 million.
